concepts.name: Distance between two points
concepts.description: The straight-line distance between two points, found using the Pythagorean relationship.

concepts.name: Midpoint of a segment
concepts.description: The point exactly halfway between two given points.

concepts.name: Slope of a line
concepts.description: How steep a line is: the rise divided by the run between any two points on it.

concepts.name: Equation of a line
concepts.description: Writing a line's equation from its slope and a point, then using it to find other points on the line.

concepts.name: Parallel and perpendicular lines
concepts.description: Parallel lines share the same slope; perpendicular lines have slopes that multiply to −1.

formulas.title: Distance formula
formulas.prompt: How do you find the distance between two points?
formulas.explanation: This is just the Pythagorean theorem applied to the horizontal and vertical gaps between the two points.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting to square the differences before adding them.

formulas.title: Midpoint formula
formulas.prompt: How do you find the midpoint of two points?
formulas.explanation: Average the x-coordinates and average the y-coordinates separately.
formulas.commonMistake: Averaging x with y instead of x with x and y with y.

formulas.title: Slope formula
formulas.prompt: How do you find the slope of a line through two points?
formulas.explanation: Keep the order of the two points consistent in both the numerator and denominator.
formulas.commonMistake: Subtracting the coordinates in a mismatched order between numerator and denominator.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Find the slope of the line through (1,1) and (5,9).

formulas.title: Equation of a line
formulas.prompt: How do you write the equation of a line from a slope and a point?
formulas.formula: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁),  which rearranges to y = mx + c
formulas.explanation: Once you know m and one point, you can find c and then evaluate y for any x on the line.
formulas.commonMistake: Substituting the point incorrectly into the point-slope formula.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A line has slope 2 and passes through (0,3). What is its equation?

formulas.title: Parallel and perpendicular slopes
formulas.prompt: How do the slopes of parallel and perpendicular lines relate?
formulas.formula:
Parallel: m₁ = m₂
Perpendicular: m₁ × m₂ = −1
formulas.explanation: A perpendicular slope is the "negative reciprocal" of the original: flip the fraction and change its sign.
formulas.example: A line with slope 3 is perpendicular to a line with slope −1/3, since 3 × (−1/3) = −1
formulas.commonMistake: Using the reciprocal without flipping the sign, or vice versa.
formulas.applicationPrompt: What slope is perpendicular to a line with slope 3?

formulas.title: Area of a triangle from its corners
formulas.prompt: How do you find the area of a triangle from three points without any lengths?
formulas.formula:
Area = ½ |x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|
Area 0 means the points are in a line
formulas.explanation: This is the shoelace formula; it needs only subtraction and multiplication.
formulas.commonMistake: Dropping the ½ or the absolute value.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Are (1, 2), (3, 6) and (5, 10) in a straight line?

formulas.title: Point dividing a segment in m : n
formulas.prompt: Where is the point dividing the line from P₁ to P₂ in the ratio m : n?
formulas.formula: ((m x₂ + n x₁) ÷ (m + n), (m y₂ + n y₁) ÷ (m + n))
formulas.explanation: Each coordinate is a weighted average, weighted towards the end it is closer to.
formulas.commonMistake: Pairing m with the first point instead of the second.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Find the point dividing (−2, 4) to (8, −1) in the ratio 3 : 2.

formulas.title: Intercept form
formulas.prompt: Where does ax + by = c cross the axes, and what triangle does it cut off?
formulas.formula:
x/p + y/q = 1 crosses at (p, 0) and (0, q)
Triangle with the axes: area ½|pq|
formulas.explanation: Divide the equation by c to read the intercepts straight off.
formulas.example: 3x + 4y = 12 is x/4 + y/3 = 1: intercepts 4 and 3, triangle area 6.
formulas.commonMistake: Reading the coefficients 3 and 4 as the intercepts.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Find the area cut off by 5x − 2y = 20 and the axes.

levels.title: Points, Distance and Midpoint
levels.description: The distance and midpoint formulas both come from the Pythagorean theorem and simple averaging.

blocks.title: Distance is just Pythagoras
blocks.body: The distance between two points is the hypotenuse of a right triangle formed by their horizontal and vertical gap. (1,2) to (4,6) has gaps of 3 and 4 — a 3-4-5 triangle, so the distance is 5.

blocks.title: Distance formula
blocks.caption: Square the gaps, add them, then take the square root.

blocks.body: The midpoint is just the average of the two x-coordinates and the average of the two y-coordinates.

questions.question: What is the distance between A(1, 2) and B(4, 6)?
questions.context: Study the points plotted on the coordinate plane and answer the question.

figure.caption: Points A(1, 2) and B(4, 6)
figure.ariaSummary: Two points, A at (1, 2) and B at (4, 6), plotted on a coordinate grid.

questions.method: Square the coordinate differences, add, then take the square root.

hints.text: This is a 3-4-5 right triangle in disguise.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to take the square root at the end.

questions.question: What is the midpoint of A(2, 3) and B(8, 7)?

figure.caption: Points A(2, 3) and B(8, 7)
figure.ariaSummary: Two points, A at (2, 3) and B at (8, 7), plotted on a coordinate grid.

questions.method: Average the x-coordinates and the y-coordinates separately.

hints.text: Average x with x, and y with y.

commonMistakes: Mixing up which coordinates to average together.

questions.question: The slope of a line through (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is
questions.explanation: Slope is "rise over run": the change in y divided by the change in x.
solutionSteps: Slope = change in y ÷ change in x.
questions.method: Rise (y) goes on top, run (x) goes on the bottom.

hints.text: "Rise over run" — y differences over x differences.

commonMistakes: Inverting the fraction, putting x differences on top.

questions.question: What is the slope of the line through A(1, 1) and B(5, 9)?

figure.caption: Line through A(1, 1) and B(5, 9)
figure.ariaSummary: A straight line through points A at (1, 1) and B at (5, 9).

questions.method: Divide the change in y by the change in x.

hints.text: Keep the point order consistent in both differences.

commonMistakes: Subtracting the coordinates in a different order for x and y.

questions.question: A line has slope 2 and passes through (0, 3). What is y when x = 4?
questions.explanation: The equation is y = 2x + 3. When x = 4: y = 2(4) + 3 = 11.
questions.method: Write the equation first, then substitute the given x.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to add the y-intercept after multiplying by the slope.

questions.question: What is the distance between A(-2, 1) and B(3, 13)?

figure.caption: Points A(-2, 1) and B(3, 13)
figure.ariaSummary: Two points, A at (-2, 1) and B at (3, 13), plotted on a coordinate grid.

questions.method: Be careful subtracting a negative x-coordinate.
commonMistakes: Mishandling the negative coordinate, using 3 − 2 = 1 instead of 5.

questions.question: A line has slope 3. Another line has slope −1/3. Are the two lines parallel, perpendicular, or neither?
questions.explanation: Multiplying the slopes: 3 × (−1/3) = −1, which means the lines are perpendicular.
questions.method: Multiply the two slopes and check if the product is −1.
commonMistakes: Assuming the lines are parallel just because the numbers look related.

questions.question: A line passes through A(2, 3) and B(6, 11). What is y when x = 10?

figure.caption: Line through A(2, 3) and B(6, 11)
figure.ariaSummary: A straight line through points A at (2, 3) and B at (6, 11).

questions.method: Find the slope first, then build the equation, then substitute.

hints.text: Find the slope before writing the equation.

commonMistakes: Using the wrong point when applying the point-slope formula.

questions.question: A triangle has vertices A(0, 0), B(6, 0) and C(3, 4). What is its perimeter?

figure.caption: Triangle with vertices A(0, 0), B(6, 0) and C(3, 4)
figure.ariaSummary: A triangle plotted on a coordinate grid with vertices A at (0, 0), B at (6, 0) and C at (3, 4).

questions.method: Find all three side lengths using the distance formula, then add them.

hints.text: Each slanted side hides a 3-4-5 right triangle.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to compute all three sides before adding.

questions.question: M(4, 1) is the midpoint of segment AB, and A = (1, -3). What are the coordinates of B?
questions.context: Study the points plotted on the coordinate plane and answer the question.

figure.caption: Endpoint A(1, -3) and midpoint M(4, 1)
figure.ariaSummary: Point A at (1, -3) joined to M at (4, 1), the midpoint of AB. B is not shown.

questions.explanation: The midpoint is the average of the endpoints, so each coordinate of B = 2 × M − A: x = 2 × 4 − 1 = 7 and y = 2 × 1 − (-3) = 5. B = (7, 5).
questions.method: Run the midpoint formula backwards: each coordinate of B = 2 × M − A.

hints.text: Write (1 + x) ÷ 2 = 4 and solve for x.

commonMistakes: Averaging A and M, which gives (2.5, -1), the midpoint of AM instead of the point B.

questions.question: Which of these lines is parallel to y = 3x − 5?
questions.explanation: Parallel lines have equal slopes. In y = mx + c the slope is m, so the line must have m = 3; only y = 3x + 2 does. A different c just shifts the line up or down.
solutionSteps: Parallel lines have the same slope, 3.

hints.text: In y = mx + c, the number multiplying x is the slope.

commonMistakes: Picking a line with the same intercept, −5, instead of the same slope.

questions.question: Point P lies on the segment from A(2, 1) to B(11, 7) and divides it internally so that AP : PB = 1 : 2. What is the x-coordinate of P?

figure.caption: Segment AB from A(2, 1) to B(11, 7)
figure.ariaSummary: A segment from A at (2, 1) to B at (11, 7). The point P that divides it is not drawn.

questions.explanation: Section formula with m : n = 1 : 2: x = (m x₂ + n x₁) ÷ (m + n) = (1 × 11 + 2 × 2) ÷ 3 = 15 ÷ 3 = 5. (P = (5, 3), one-third of the way from A to B.)
questions.method: Apply the section formula, weighting each endpoint by the opposite part of the ratio.

hints.text: AP : PB = 1 : 2 puts P one-third of the way from A to B.
From x = 2 to x = 11 is 9 units; take one-third of that.

commonMistakes: Swapping the weights, which gives (2 × 11 + 1 × 2) ÷ 3 = 8, the point two-thirds of the way.

questions.question: The line through A(2, k) and B(5, 9) is perpendicular to the line 2x + 3y = 6. Find k.
questions.explanation: Rewrite 2x + 3y = 6 as y = −(2/3)x + 2, so its slope is −2/3. A perpendicular line has slope 3/2, because the product of the slopes is −1. Then (9 − k) ÷ (5 − 2) = 3/2, so 9 − k = 4.5 and k = 4.5.
questions.method: Find the given slope, take its negative reciprocal, then solve the slope equation for k.
commonMistakes: Reading the slope of 2x + 3y = 6 as 2 or 2/3, forgetting the minus sign.
Using the same slope (parallel lines) instead of the negative reciprocal.
